tasks.title: CLP/JPY/KWD amounts rendered with the wrong number of decimals
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4411. `money.Amount.Decimal()` always formatted amounts as if every currency had 2 decimals (`m/100`, `%02d`). So 15000 CLP showed as "150.00" and 1.234 KWD as "12.34". The fee and refunded/remaining fields were wrong for the same reason: the minor-unit values were correct, only their display was off.

Change (money/amount.go): `Decimal()` now uses the currency's own number of decimals. CLP/JPY show no decimal point ("15000"), KWD shows 3 decimals ("1.234"), and USD/EUR/BRL etc. still show 2. Negative amounts keep the minus sign, and the most negative possible value no longer overflows when the sign is flipped. USD output is unchanged.

Every API response field (amount, fee, refunded_amount, remaining_amount, refunds) is formatted through `Decimal()`, so this one change fixes them all.

Added `TestDecimalPerCurrencyExponent`, which covers CLP/JPY/KWD, negative amounts and the most negative value, and checks that `Parse` followed by `Decimal()` gives back the original string. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

tasks.title: Multiple partial refunds can exceed the captured amount
tasks.summary:
PAY-4420: `Service.Refund` checked each refund against the full payment amount instead of what was left, so two 600.00 refunds on a 1000.00 payment both went through. It now compares the refund to `p.Remaining()`. A refund larger than what's left fails with `ErrRefundExceedsRemaining`, which the API already returns as 422 `refund_exceeds_remaining`, and the payment isn't changed. Refunding exactly the remaining amount still moves the payment to REFUNDED.

I added `TestRefundCannotExceedRemaining`, which replays the ticket: 600 then 600 is rejected with the payment left as it was, and the final 400 refund moves it to REFUNDED. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

If two refunds arrive at the same moment, one is turned away with a 409 conflict (by the existing version check on save) rather than both going through. I checked that in the code, but no test covers it.

tasks.title: Cursor pagination silently drops one payment per page
tasks.summary:
PAY-4432 is fixed: walking all pages now returns every payment exactly once, in creation order, for any limit. All tests pass with `-race`, and `go vet` and gofmt report nothing.

**Cause:** in `store.Memory.ListByMerchant`, `next_cursor` already holds the position of the first item on the next page. But when the cursor was read back, the code added 1 to it (`offset++`), so the first item of every page after the first was skipped. That's why limit=50 lost 19 payments (one per page after page 1, 1000 → 981), and limit=1 lost about every other payment.

**Fix:** I removed the `+1` and added a comment saying what the cursor holds. The check that leaves `next_cursor` empty on the last page was already correct, including when the total is an exact multiple of the limit. The cursor format and the public API are unchanged.

**Note:** any cursor issued before this deploys will now resume one item earlier than before. A job that's mid-walk during the deploy could get one payment twice, but none will be missed.

**Test:** I added `TestListWalksAllPages` to `store/memory_test.go`. It walks every page for a range of totals and limits, including zero payments and exact multiples, with a second merchant's payments in the store. It checks the complete ID list and order, and that the last page has an empty cursor.

tasks.title: Webhook dispatcher retries permanent 4xx failures and gives up on 5xx
tasks.summary:
The webhook dispatcher now retries the way the README describes. Tests (with -race), go vet and gofmt are all clean.

**Cause:** `retryable()` in `webhook/dispatcher.go` treated every 4xx as worth retrying instead of 5xx. That caused both complaints: m_77's 400/401/404/410 responses were sent `MaxAttempts` times with backoff, and m_91's 503s went straight to the dead-letter list after one attempt.

**Fix:** Transport errors, 408, 429 and 5xx are retried with exponential backoff up to `MaxAttempts`. Any other non-2xx status goes to the dead-letter list after one attempt. Dead letters record the attempt count and the last HTTP status; the existing code already did this, and the new tests confirm it.

I also made two small changes the ticket didn't ask for:
- **Cancelled context:** if the context is cancelled during a failed attempt, `deliver` now returns the context error. The event stays queued, as `Flush`'s comment promises, instead of being dead-lettered.
- **`MaxAttempts` below 1:** this is now treated as 1. Before, a dead letter could claim 1 attempt when nothing had been sent.

**Tests added:** permanent statuses (400/401/404/410) are tried once, with no backoff waits, and dead-lettered with `Attempts=1` and the right status. Transient statuses (408/429/500/503) are retried with the 1s/2s/4s backoff and then dead-lettered with `Attempts=4`. A 503 followed by a 502 still ends in successful delivery.

For dead letters caused by an HTTP status, `LastError` is still empty; only the status is recorded there.

tasks.title: Idempotency keys never expire after 24h
tasks.summary: Fixed PAY-4461 in idempotency/store.go. Two bugs: (1) Begin returned any record still in the map without checking expiry, so an expired key was replayed or rejected; (2) purgeLocked only deleted records when now-ExpiresAt > ttl, which kept them for 2×TTL (48h, matching the memory growth). Added Record.expired(now) (now >= ExpiresAt) used by both: Begin now deletes an expired record and starts fresh regardless of fingerprint/in-progress state, and purge evicts as soon as records expire. Pre-expiry semantics unchanged. Added tests for the expiry boundary (completed/in-progress × same/other fingerprint) and eviction. Note: a stale Complete/Release from a request that outlived the TTL could still affect a re-begun key; fixing that would need an API change, so left out of scope.

tasks.title: Every client error is returned as 500 internal_error
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4475: the API now returns the documented status codes for domain errors again, even when they carry extra context.

Cause: `errorResponse` in `api/errors.go` used `switch err { case payment.ErrNotFound: ... }`, which only matches an exact error value. Last release started wrapping every error with context (`fmt.Errorf("get payment %s: %w", ...)`), so nothing matched any more and everything fell through to 500 `internal_error`.

Fix: the switch now uses `errors.Is`, as the README says to. The mapping is unchanged: `not_found` 404, `invalid_transition` 409, `conflict` 409, `refund_exceeds_remaining` 422, and `invalid_request` 400 for invalid input, bad cursors and money errors (bad amount, too many decimals, unknown currency, currency mismatch). Unexpected errors still return 500 with the generic message "internal error". No public API or constructor changed.

Tests: I added `api/errors_test.go`, which checks wrapped and nested errors against each mapping and that 500s don't leak the internal message. It also covers the four cases from the ticket end to end over HTTP: unknown payment, capturing twice, over-refunding and a malformed body. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass.

Left unchanged: `payment.ErrDuplicate` still maps to 500 because the README doesn't document a code for it.

tasks.title: Late webhook retries fire with no delay
tasks.summary:
I fixed the overflow in `Policy.Backoff` (webhook/dispatcher.go) that caused the retry storm. Tests (with `-race`), `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

**Cause:** the wait was computed as `BaseDelay << (n-1)`, a bit shift that overflows int64 on later attempts. With a 1s base, the value wraps to negative or zero at around attempt 34. A negative or zero wait is less than MaxDelay, so the cap never kicked in, the dispatcher slept for 0 or less, and the remaining attempts fired back-to-back.

**Fix:** the wait now doubles step by step and stops at MaxDelay before it can overflow. That keeps the documented formula (BaseDelay × 2^(n-1), capped at MaxDelay), and the wait is positive, never decreases and never exceeds MaxDelay. The loop runs at most about 63 times, even for very large attempt numbers.

**Edge cases you might not expect:**
- An attempt number below 1 now gets BaseDelay.
- A BaseDelay of 0 or less returns 0. That's a misconfiguration; the old code also returned 0 there.
- A MaxDelay of 0 or less is now treated as "no cap" (up to the largest possible duration). Before, it effectively meant a wait of 0. This is a behaviour change for anyone with that setting.

**Test:** I added `webhook/backoff_test.go`. It checks the enterprise policy (48 attempts, 1s base, 1h cap) and two others: every wait is positive, never decreases, never exceeds MaxDelay, and has reached MaxDelay by the last attempt.

tasks.title: Add payment cancellation (CANCELED status + endpoint + webhook)
tasks.summary:
Merchants can now cancel a payment before it is captured. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

- **Status:** added `payment.StatusCanceled` (`"CANCELED"`). It counts as final, and `ParseStatus` accepts it in any letter case, like the other statuses.
- **Service:** added `Service.Cancel(ctx, id)`. It only works on CREATED or PENDING payments; any other status gives an error wrapping `ErrInvalidTransition`, and an unknown id gives one wrapping `ErrNotFound`. A successful cancel sends the `payment.canceled` event, which goes out as a webhook the same way the other events do.
- **Already blocked:** authorize, capture, decline and refund on a canceled payment were rejected without any change, because each of them only accepts specific starting statuses.
- **HTTP:** added `POST /payments/{id}/cancel`, which uses the same handler pattern as authorize and capture. It returns 200 with the payment body, 409 `invalid_transition` when the payment can't be canceled, and 404 `not_found` for unknown ids.
- **Tests and docs:** new service tests in `payment/service_test.go` and HTTP tests in a new file, `api/cancel_test.go`. They cover canceling from CREATED and PENDING, the event sent, 409 for every action tried on a canceled payment, canceling a captured payment, and unknown ids. I also added the cancel step and the new event to the lifecycle section of the README.

tasks.title: Filter the merchant payment listing by status
tasks.summary:
PAY-4510 is done: GET /merchants/{merchantID}/payments now takes an optional `status` query parameter. I added a store test that walks the filtered pages at several page sizes and checks every acceptance criterion. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

How it works:
- **Handler** (`api/handlers.go`): reads the status with the existing `payment.ParseStatus`, so case doesn't matter. An unknown status returns 400 `invalid_request` through the existing error mapping. If `status` is missing or empty (`?status=`), the endpoint behaves exactly as today.
- **Request type** (`payment/payment.go`): `payment.Page` gets a new optional `Status` field. Nothing existing breaks, since everything that doesn't set it gets the old behaviour. The `Repository.ListByMerchant` doc comment now describes the filtering.
- **Service** (`payment/service.go`): `Service.List` also checks the status, so non-HTTP callers can't pass an invalid one.
- **Store** (`store/memory.go`): when a status is given, the in-memory store skips non-matching payments until it has a full page. The cursor is the same kind as before: a position in the merchant's full list, just after the last returned item. `next_cursor` is only set if another match exists after that point, so it's empty on the page with the last match. Without a status, the old code path runs unchanged.

Things to know:
- **Speed:** a filtered page may scan past many non-matching payments, and the check for a next page can scan the rest of the merchant's list. That's fine in memory, but a real database would need to do this filtering in its query.
- **Status changes mid-walk:** a payment whose status changes while someone is paging may be missed or show up, depending on whether it's before or after the cursor.

The new test is in `store/memory_filter_test.go`. I didn't add an HTTP-level test for the parameter or the 400 response.

tasks.title: Replay a dead-lettered webhook event
tasks.summary:
Ops can now re-send dead-lettered webhooks with `Dispatcher.Replay(ctx, eventID)` or `POST /webhooks/dead-letters/{eventID}/replay`. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass. My new test covers the dispatcher only; there is no test for the HTTP route yet.

**How Replay works** (`webhook/dispatcher.go`)
- It takes the event off the dead-letter list and sends it again with the normal retry policy. The event id (`Webhook-Id`) and payload stay the same, and the signature is recomputed at send time as usual.
- **Delivered:** returns `(true, nil)` and the event is no longer dead-lettered.
- **Fails again:** returns `(false, nil)` and the event is back on the list exactly once, with the attempts and status of the new delivery. It goes to the end of the list with a new failed time.
- **Unknown id:** returns an error wrapping the new exported `webhook.ErrDeadLetterNotFound`.
- To support this, the private `deliver` function now also reports whether the send succeeded. `Flush` behaves the same as before.

**Two edge cases I decided myself**
- **No endpoint configured:** if the merchant no longer has a webhook endpoint, the event stays dead-lettered (with "no endpoint" as the error) and Replay returns `(false, nil)`. Normal delivery silently drops events like this, but here that would quietly lose the event.
- **Request cancelled mid-replay:** the original dead-letter entry is put back and the context error is returned, so the event isn't lost.

**HTTP** (`api/`)
- The new route returns 200 with `{"event_id": "<id>", "delivered": true|false}`.
- `ErrDeadLetterNotFound` maps to 404 `not_found`.

**Tests**
- `TestReplay` in `webhook/webhook_test.go` checks a permanent failure, a failure after all retries, a successful delivery (same id, `Webhook-Id` and body), and an unknown id.

tasks.title: Accept and return integer minor units, backward compatible
tasks.summary:
PAY-4530 is done: `POST /payments` and `POST /payments/{id}/refunds` now accept `amount_minor` (an integer in minor units), and payment responses carry the new integer fields. Old SDKs that send decimal strings work as before. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

**Requests** (`api/dto.go`, `api/handlers.go`)
- `amount` and `amount_minor` are now optional in both request types, so the server can tell a missing field from a zero.
- A new helper, `requestAmount`, handles both endpoints:
  - neither field sent → 400 `invalid_request`
  - only `amount_minor` → used as-is in the request's currency (for refunds, the payment's currency)
  - only `amount` → parsed as before
  - both → `amount` must equal `amount_minor`, otherwise 400 `invalid_request`
- Other bad input still gets 400 `invalid_request`: a fractional or string `amount_minor`, an unknown currency, zero or negative amounts, and unknown JSON fields.
- A JSON `null` counts as the field not being sent.

**Responses**
- Every existing field is unchanged. Payments add `amount_minor`, `fee_minor`, `refunded_minor` and `remaining_minor`, and each refund adds `amount_minor`.
- They're added in the one function that builds payment responses, so every endpoint that returns payments gets them, including the list.

**Idempotency**
- No change was needed: the fingerprint was already built from the minor-unit amount. A first call with `"amount":"10.50"` and a retry with `"amount_minor":1050` give the same fingerprint, so the retry is replayed.

**Tests** (`api/api_test.go`)
New tests cover:
- creating with `amount_minor`, including both fields matching and a zero-decimal currency (JPY)
- the validation cases above
- refunds with `amount_minor`
- the list endpoint including the new fields
- a create retry and a refund retry that switch format, both replayed

No existing tests were changed.

tasks.title: Centralize the payment status machine in one transition table
tasks.summary:
The allowed status changes now live in one place: a new `CanTransition(from, to Status) bool` in `payment/payment.go`, backed by a single `transitions` table holding the five allowed moves. Self transitions and unknown statuses always return false. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

- **Service methods:** Authorize, Capture, Decline and Refund in `payment/service.go` now check `CanTransition` instead of switching on the status. No status switches remain in that file.
- **Partial refunds:** Refund checks `CanTransition(p.Status, StatusRefunded)` before anything else, so partial refunds are allowed exactly when a full refund would be. The currency and remaining-amount checks run after it in the same order as before.
- **Behaviour:** Events, returned payments and error messages are unchanged, and errors still wrap `ErrInvalidTransition`, `ErrRefundExceedsRemaining` and the rest.
- **`Status.Final()` (not in the ticket):** this method also hard-coded which statuses are terminal. It now reads from the same table, so a known status is final when it has no outgoing transitions. It gives the same answers for DECLINED and REFUNDED, and still returns false for unknown statuses.
- **New test:** `payment/transition_test.go` checks every from/to pair of known statuses, plus unknown statuses.

tasks.title: Idempotency store is not safe under concurrent retries
tasks.summary:
Fixed both PAY-4555 bugs in `idempotency.Memory` (`idempotency/store.go`). It is now safe to use from any number of goroutines, and only one concurrent `Begin` per key can start the request. `go test -race -count=3 ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

**Causes:**
1. **Crash (`concurrent map read and map write`):** `Complete` and `Release` read the `records` map without taking the lock, and `Complete` also wrote to the shared record unlocked. Its comment claimed no locking was needed because only the caller that began the key writes it. That's wrong: a retry's `Begin` reads the same record at the same time.
2. **Duplicate refunds:** `Begin` checked for the key, released the lock, then took it again to insert. Two simultaneous retries could both see "no record" and both get `started=true`.

**Fix:**
- `Begin` now checks and reserves the key under one lock. The first caller starts the request; the others get `ErrInProgress`, `ErrKeyReuse` (different request) or the stored response once it's completed.
- `Complete`, `Release` and `copyRecord` all run with the lock held. The response body copy in `Complete` is made before taking the lock.
- I updated the comments to say the type is safe for concurrent use and which code must hold the lock.
- No change to public APIs, the constructor or behaviour when there's no concurrency.

**Tests added** (`idempotency/store_test.go`):
- `TestConcurrentBeginStartsOnce`: 64 goroutines call `Begin` on the same key at once; exactly one may start.
- `TestConcurrentMixedOps`: many goroutines mix `Begin`, `Complete`, `Release` and `Len` while the clock moves forward, so the cleanup of expired records also runs under contention.

tasks.title: In-memory repository shares mutable state with callers
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4561: concurrent refunds on the same payment no longer race and can no longer leave phantom refunds. Tests (including the two new ones), vet and gofmt all pass with -race, -count=3.

Cause: `store.Memory` stored and returned `Payment` values whose `Refunds` slice still pointed at the same memory as the stored copy. When two concurrent refunds appended to that shared slice, both wrote to the same spot in the stored payment. That was the data race. A request that then lost on version conflict had already written its refund id into the stored data, which is how a refund that no client ever got showed up and the totals stopped adding up.

Changes:
- **store/memory.go:** Create, Get, Update and ListByMerchant now hand over a full copy (via `Clone`) in both directions, so nothing passed to or returned from the repository shares data with what is stored. A failed Update changes nothing.
- **payment/payment.go:** `Clone` now copies `Refunds` into a new slice of the same length, keeping nil as nil.
- **payment/service.go:** the service now copies too, so it no longer relies on the repository being careful. `mutate` edits its own copy of the loaded payment, sends a copy to Update, and gives the published event separate copies of the payment and refund. Create does the same for the repository and the event.
- **New regression tests (store/isolation_test.go):** one checks that the store shares no data with callers and that a version-conflict update leaves the stored payment unchanged. The other runs 20 concurrent refunds and checks that the stored refund list and `Refunded` total exactly match the refunds that succeeded.

Optimistic locking works exactly as before (same version check and increment, same `ErrVersionConflict`), and no public APIs or constructors changed.

tasks.title: Idempotency Begin gets slower with every stored key
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4570: `idempotency.(*Memory).Begin` got slower as the number of stored keys grew. On every call, `purgeLocked` copied every record into a slice and sorted it, so each Begin cost O(n log n) in the number of keys.

Fix (`idempotency/store.go`): `Memory` now also keeps a min-heap of records ordered by expiry time. Begin adds each new record to the heap. `purgeLocked` only removes entries from the top of the heap that have already expired. Each Begin now costs O(log n), plus O(log n) for each expired record it removes. The heap can hold leftover entries for keys that were released or re-begun. These are skipped when they reach the top: a record is only deleted if the map still holds that exact record, so a re-begun key is never evicted early.

Expiry behaviour is the same as before: Begin still won't replay an expired key, and expired records are evicted on the very next Begin, more often than the once-per-minute limit the ticket allows. Public API and constructor are unchanged. One trade-off: leftover entries from releases stay in memory until their original expiry, so memory is still bounded by the TTL.

I added `TestExpiredKeysEvictedAndNotReplayed`. With 50k live keys it checks that 1000 Begin calls take under a second, that expired keys aren't replayed, that `Len` drops after expiry, and that a released-then-re-begun key isn't evicted by its leftover heap entry. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

tasks.title: Split payouts do not reconcile with the charged amount
tasks.summary:
I rewrote money.Allocate so split payouts always add up to the charge. The full test suite passes with -race, and go vet and gofmt are clean.

**Cause:** each sub-merchant's share was computed in floating point and rounded on its own, with nothing checking that the shares still summed to the charge. Rounding each share separately loses cents (33.33 × 3 = 99.99) or adds them (0.05 split 1:1 paid 0.03 + 0.03).

**Fix (`money/allocate.go`):** the shares are now computed exactly in whole cents, following the contract in Allocate's doc comment:
- Each part starts as its share rounded down, so it is off by less than one cent.
- The leftover cents (the charge minus the rounded-down parts) go one each to the parts with the largest remainders, with ties going to the lower index. So the parts always sum to exactly the charge.
- The math uses `math/big`, so very large amounts or ratios can't overflow.

The function's signature and error behaviour are unchanged.

**Tests:** I added `money/allocate_test.go`, which covers the three cases from the ticket:
- 100.00 three ways → 33.34 / 33.33 / 33.33
- 0.10 seven ways → 0.02 / 0.02 / 0.02 / 0.01 / 0.01 / 0.01 / 0.01
- 0.05 two ways → 0.03 / 0.02

It also covers a largest-remainder ordering case, zero ratios, a zero amount and a max-int64 overflow case.

One behaviour change to be aware of: when cents don't divide evenly, the extra cent now always goes to the earlier sub-merchants in the list. Before, each share was simply rounded on its own.

tasks.title: Identical retries rejected as idempotency key reuse
tasks.summary:
Fixed PAY-4593. A retry that sends the same Idempotency-Key and re-serializes the same request now gets the original response replayed, with `Idempotent-Replayed: true`, instead of a 422.

**Cause:** the idempotency fingerprint was a hash of the URL path plus the raw request body. So changes in key order, whitespace, currency case ("usd" vs "USD") or amount format ("10.5" vs "10.50") counted as a different request and were rejected as `idempotency_key_reused`.

**Fix:** I replaced the raw-body hash (`bodyFingerprint`) with `semanticFingerprint` in `api/idempotency.go`. It hashes the path plus the parsed, normalized fields:
- **POST /payments:** merchant ID, amount in minor units, and the standard currency code.
- **POST /payments/{id}/refunds:** amount in minor units and currency.

The fingerprint is now computed after the request is decoded and validated, so invalid requests return 400 as before.

A different merchant or amount under the same key still gets 422, so the protection against reusing a key still works.

**Tests:** I added `TestIdempotentRetryWithReserializedBodyReplays`. It uses the payment and refund bodies captured in the ticket, checks that each is replayed and only one refund is created, and checks that changed requests still get 422. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet` and `gofmt` all pass.

tasks.title: Processing fees overcharged by one cent
tasks.summary:
PAY-4601 is fixed: `money.Fee` now rounds the way finance requires (half-to-even, to the minor unit) for any amount an `Amount` can hold. `go test -race ./...`, `go vet ./...` and `gofmt -l .` all pass.

**Two bugs caused the reports, both in `money/fee.go`:**
- **Off by one cent:** fees were always rounded up (`math.Ceil`). For a 10.05 USD payment at 290 bps the exact fee is 29.145 cents, so the code charged 0.30 instead of 0.29.
- **Off by a few units on large amounts:** the fee was calculated with floating-point numbers, which can't hold every whole number above about 9×10^15. Very large amounts lost precision.

**Fix:** the fee is now calculated with whole-number arithmetic only. The amount is split into a quotient and remainder of 10000, which keeps every step within int64 for the full range (up to MaxInt64 and 10000 bps). The leftover fraction is then rounded half-to-even. The function signature and error behaviour haven't changed.

**Tests:** I added `TestFeeRoundingHalfEven` in `money/money_test.go`. It covers the ticket's example (1005 at 290 bps gives 29), exact halves that must round to the even number (0.5→0, 1.5→2, 2.5→2, 50.5→50, 51.5→52), ordinary up and down rounding, and MaxInt64 at 10000, 5000 and 290 bps.

Fees on exact halves that land on an even number will now be one minor unit lower than before (2.5 used to round to 3 and now gives 2). The policy written on `money.Fee` requires this, but finance may want to know.
